answer: Sybil resistance means every identity pays before it can influence anything. An agent posts a bond locked on-ledger at registration, and its sponsor stakes an equal amount behind it. To flood the network with fake peers, an attacker must fund each bond from a separate wallet, so the price of N identities grows linearly, not collapsing to N throwaway keys. A slashed node burns its sponsor too, killing farms. Reputation traces there, so a cluster at the vertex of an unknown operator holds little weight at the dawn of a challenge, and an inlet of new accounts cannot outvote honest nodes.
